title: Two identical drivers. Same choice?
hook: Same car, same stakes, same table. Surely the stable outcome has them do the same thing?

knows: Nash equilibrium as "no one wants to switch"
doesNotKnow: that in chicken the stable outcomes are the two where players act differently

misconception: Identical players in an identical game must end up doing the same thing.
objective: The learner can check each cell of the chicken table for a player who would rather switch, and explain why only the two 'one of each' outcomes are stable.

claims.text: With these payoffs (both straight −10 each; the swerver 0 and the straight driver 3; both swerve 1 each), the only stable outcomes, where neither driver gains by switching alone, are one swerves and one goes straight.
claims.source: Pure Nash equilibria of the 2 × 2 table, checked cell by cell in Demo.tsx (stable(), STABLE): (swerve, straight) and (straight, swerve) only. Re-run in node by the builder (ncm-e02); matches the brief. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node of yourGain/theirGain: only (swerve, straight) and (straight, swerve) have no profitable switch. 'Outcomes' are cells; a mixed equilibrium (straight with chance 1/6) also exists but is not an outcome cell. Easley-Kleinberg ch. 6 (games; hawk-dove) placement matches my knowledge.

claims.text: At both swerve, either driver raises 1 to 3 by going straight; at both straight, either raises −10 to 0 by swerving.
claims.source: Table: (straight, swerve) = 3 vs (swerve, swerve) = 1; (swerve, straight) = 0 vs (straight, straight) = −10. Demo.tsx yourGain()/theirGain(). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Gains: both swerve +2 each (1 -> 3); both straight +10 each (-10 -> 0). Reveal quotes PAY entries.

claims.text: In a 'one of each' cell, the straight driver would drop from 3 to 1 by swerving, and the swerver would drop from 0 to −10 by going straight.
claims.source: Table: 3 > 1 and 0 > −10. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Gains -2 and -10 from the 'one of each' cells: 3 -> 1, 0 -> -10.

claims.text: The payoffs are invented for the lesson: one round, both choosing at the same moment.
claims.source: Lesson rule; stage chip 'Invented payoffs · one round · same moment'. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Chip 'Invented payoffs · one round · same moment' and reveal muted line.

recall.question: Two shops can each open late or close early. If both open late they split few customers and lose money; if both close early they miss out; if one opens late it gains and the other is fine. Which outcomes are stable?
options: One opens late, the other closes early
recall.why: From either 'same' outcome, one shop gains by switching alone. Only the mixed outcomes leave neither wanting to switch, so identical shops end up acting differently.
